validation.source_citation: Perry, R.H. & Green, D.W. (eds.), Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook, 8th ed. (2008), Table 2-319 Viscosity of Sucrose Solutions, 20 wt% at 20 degC = 1.967 mPa s. Viscosity tolerance is 3% because published solution-viscosity data and the correlation's viscosity term carry larger uncertainty than density.
validation.source_title: Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook, 8th ed. - Viscosity of Sucrose Solutions

validity_note: Laliberte (2009) aqueous-solution correlation applied to sucrose-water; sucrose is a non-electrolyte molecular solute that the correlation covers with density and viscosity coefficients. Tabulated for 5-50 wt% over 15-55 degC, within the correlation's fitted window (density and viscosity to about 50.7 wt% and 15-55 degC). Degrees Brix is shown as a derived column because, by definition, deg Bx equals wt% sucrose (grams of sucrose per 100 g of solution). Heat capacity is not tabulated: the correlation carries no sucrose heat-capacity coefficients, so it is omitted rather than faked. Sucrose is highly soluble (about 67 wt% at 20 degC), so the 50 wt% ceiling stays below saturation. Values are for preliminary design; verify against vendor data for critical service.
